subject: Elara Health onboarding — cost & performance tuning charter
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@elarahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.m@elarahealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T16:12:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff + workload snapshot

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Elara is excited to move to the implementation phase. Attaching a small production workload snapshot so your team can size the initial tuning sprint. High-level asks from our side:
- Reduce average per-request cost by ~30% (baseline: our current LLM spend)
- Keep 95th percentile latency under 350ms for chat endpoints
- Preserve top-line SLA for clinical prompt quality (we'll share eval sets)

Would like a short charter/plan that outlines batching/caching strategy, recommended quantization profile, and routing/fallback policies so we can align procurement and engineering. Can we kick off the technical handoff the week of Oct 4?

Attachments: [elara_production_workload_snapshot.csv (csv, 2.1MB)]

Best,
Sam
Customer Success Manager, Elara Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-29T09:08:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff + workload snapshot

Sam — thanks for the snapshot and clear goals. Monica will lead the tuning sprint and Rachel will run success metrics & procurement alignment. Below is a concise "cost/perf tuning charter" we propose for the Oct 4 technical kickoff:

Objectives (first 2-week sprint):
- Establish baseline metrics (tokens/sec, cost/request, p50/p95 latency) using your snapshot and a small live traffic replay.
- Implement continuous batching for short chat requests; initial batching target: 8-12 requests per batch given your request size distribution.
- Evaluate prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts and common user intents (covering ~35% of sessions).
- Test two quantization profiles: q4_k (low-memory, medium-accuracy) and int8 (aggressive size reduction). We'll measure quality on your eval suite.
- Define routing policy: primary -> high-accuracy instance (q4_k) for long-form, fallback -> quantized instance for bursts or cost-sensitive routes.

Deliverables by Oct 16:
- Batching & cache config (yaml) + perf runbook
- Quantization comparison report (accuracy delta + cost/capacity delta)
- Canary rollout plan + rollback criteria
- Rough cost delta estimate for production (low/med/high scenarios)

Action items before kickoff:
1) Sam: confirm Oct 4 10:00am ET for a 60-minute technical kickoff (we'll send invite).
2) Sam: share any additional eval prompt sets and live-replay access (S3 or Drive).
3) Monica: prepare batching_profile_template.yaml and SOW draft.
4) Rachel: prepare procurement checklist and estimate cadence for Reserved capacity decision.

Attachments: [SOW_draft_v2.docx]

I'll send a calendar invite and a short agenda. Looking forward — Karthik

Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Sam Torres <sam.torres@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T11:46:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff + workload snapshot

Thanks — added a technical checklist below so the kickoff is actionable. I'm listing what I will validate in sprint 1 and what I need from Elara beforehand.

Sprint-1 technical checklist (owner: Monica):
- Ingest workload snapshot into staging and run replay harness to get baseline p50/p95 and token mix.
- Batching config: start with target_batch_size=10, max_batch_latency=30ms; monitor tail latency impact and adjust.
- Caching: enable prefix KV caching for session-start templates; measure hit-rate and cold-start penalty.
- Quantization: produce two artifacts — model_q4_k and model_int8. Run 500-sample eval on clinical prompts, measure exact-match/F1 and human-review flags.
- Routing policy: implement policy file with three tiers (accurate, balanced, cheap) and an automated fallback to 'balanced' when queue length > threshold.
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic -> 20% -> 50% with automatic rollback on quality regression (>3% failure on eval set) or latency SLA breach.

Requirements from Elara before Oct 4:
- Shared eval prompt set + labels (https link accepted).
- Short list of top 25 user intents and example utterances.
- Temporary credentials for a read-only S3 bucket with replay payloads.

Technical notes / quick estimations:
- If the workload has a high fraction of short-turn chat (median tokens/request < 60), batching will likely yield 20-35% token-efficiency gain.
- q4_k usually gives ~2.5-3x memory reduction with <5% quality degradation vs fp16 in many instruction-finetuned models; int8 is more variable but can cut cost further for non-clinical heavy paths.

Attachment: [batching_profile_template.yaml]

I'll bring a short demo of the replay harness to the kickoff. Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@elarahealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Priya Menon <priya.m@elarahealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T08:22:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff + workload snapshot

On Thu, Sep 30, 2026 at 11:46 AM Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks — added a technical checklist below so the kickoff is actionable. I'm listing what I will validate in sprint 1 and what I need from Elara beforehand.

Thanks Monica — this is exactly the level of detail we need. Quick updates:
- Eval set (redacted) uploaded to the Drive folder you listed: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Elara-Onboard
- S3 read-only credentials attached to the SOW folder in Drive (see internal note).
- We confirm Oct 4 10:00am ET for the kickoff.

Two quick questions ahead of the meeting:
1) Can you provide a ballpark of expected cost reduction if batching + q4_k are both applied? Even a conservative range helps procurement.
2) What constraints should we expect for clinical prompts (safety/human-in-loop) that would prevent aggressive quantization?

Attachment: [elara_eval_prompts.json (json, 1.8MB)]

Appreciate it — Sam

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@elarahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:35:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff + workload snapshot (agenda + invite)

Sam / team — quick follow-up before our kickoff in 25 minutes. Short answers to your questions: 

1) Conservative cost-savings estimate (first-phase): batching + q4_k -> approx 18-28% lower per-request token compute cost in typical chat workloads; end-to-end production savings depends on cache effectiveness and traffic shaping (we'll produce low/med/high scenarios in Sprint 1 deliverable).
2) Clinical prompt constraints: avoid aggressive quantization for any prompt types that require exact token-level fidelity for safety-critical outputs (e.g., dosing guidance). Those should be routed to the accurate tier (fp16 / q4_k depending on eval). We will identify those intents in the "top 25" list.

Decisions / owners (confirmed):
- Monica: technical tuning & replay runs (owner).
- Rachel: procurement cadence & SOW finalization (owner).
- Karthik: product-ops escalation and rollout gating.

Next steps: Monica will share a public sprint-1 runbook after the kickoff; Rachel will confirm reserved capacity intake timeline. I'll post the meeting notes and a short action tracker to the HubSpot deal.

See you on the call.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
